text_fidelity_a:
APC External Battery Pack, BR24BPG, Supplemental Battery for UPS Model BR1500G (Sold Separately) this has nothing within Amazon's control! I have used APC UPSs at work for years and found them dependable, reliable for my 350+ server environment. Maybe their quality control doesn't extend to their consumer product line. upon install and following all instructions the battery failed self test, really!?!? it was manufactured 9/2103 passes their internal QA per document included in package but fails 3 months later????

update: 1/27/2014
did chat with APC support. I was told I should have plugged in UPS and charged battery for 16 hours PRIOR to attempting to put a load on it. NOTHING I have read in the accompanying documents even hinted to that. I am skeptical, but will do as instructed for process of elimination in troubleshooting this problem. I told the support rep that this little bit of information should be passed on to the END USER SOME HOW!! I will update this review as I go through the resolution of this issue.

update 1/29/2014
So I did what APC said and took the load off and charged the UPS for 24 hrs (I figured a little extra wouldn't hurt). Installed the UPS and placed a load on it (~35%), performed the self-test and it passed. This KEY IMPORTANT fact should be SOMEWHERE in the included documentation, it would help everyone! I did increase my rating since the product now works as described, not happy about the lack of documentation and extra hassle required kept my ratings from being higher.
text_fidelity_b: APC External Battery Pack, BR24BPG, Supplemental Battery for UPS Model BR1500G (Sold Separately)

text_fidelity_a:
Tiffen 82VND 82 Millimeter Variable ND Filter Shooting video outdoors with a DSLR requires, obviously, proper exposure. When shooting at 24 (23.978) frames per second, the normal shutter speed should be 1/50th of a second (1/60 at 29.97 fps). If the camera is set at the lowest ISO rating of 100, in bright daylight the f/stop would be around f/22. If you want to operate at wider aperture to achieve shallow depth of field, you need to cut the light.

This variable density filter allows such an adjustment. The problem is that it cuts the light by rotating two polarizing filters against each other. Polarizers can be tricky and, by design, modify the quality of light. Thus it may act unexpectedly.

One downside is that the front of the filter is not threaded and my 77mm model is a larger diameter than the 70-200mm Nikon zoom it fits on. So now the bayonet lens hood won't fit. Now I'm outdoors with a filter on the lens and no hood to block flare. There aren't any hoods that naturally fit the filter so you need to tape a hood to the outer ring or use a matte box.
text_fidelity_b: Tiffen 82VND 82 Millimeter Variable ND Filter

text_fidelity_a:
TECKNET Wireless Mouse, 2.4G Ergonomic Optical Mouse, Computer Mouse for Laptop, PC, Computer, Chromebook, Notebook, 6 Buttons, 24 Months Battery Life, 2600 DPI, 5 Adjustment Levels I've used several mice before, and this is without a doubt the most uncomfortable mouse I've ever put my hands on. My hands are pretty small for a guy, and I was looking for something to replace my Logitech M705 that died. This mouse looks almost identical, if not better. However, I noticed immediately after putting batteries in it (none came with it) and plugging the dongle into the computer that there was a slight lag in comparison to the low quality wired Dell mouse I've been using temporarily. I can deal with a slight delay, especially since the movement didn't appear choppy, just delayed. The second thing I noticed was how poorly placed the forward/backward buttons are. You cannot avoid the buttons, and are forced to either rest you thumb on the buttons or on the desk, which I find uncomfortable. The "Ergonomic" design of the mouse was poorly designed and does not fit in your hand well at all--no matter what position I held the mouse, there was a constant pressure on my thumb, and I could never completely grip the mouse. I tried getting used to it, and used it for maybe an hour before becoming furious with how uncomfortable it is in my hands. I now have a mouse that will never be used and will likely donate it, since you cannot return it. I should have just gone with the Logitech. Yet another victim to high ratings and low cost.

tl;dr Do not get this mouse.
text_fidelity_b: TECKNET Wireless Mouse, 2.4G Ergonomic Optical Mouse, Computer Mouse for Laptop, PC, Computer, Chromebook, Notebook, 6 Buttons, 24 Months Battery Life, 2600 DPI, 5 Adjustment Levels

The camera's video quality is great. I currently have Ring and the quality of this camera beat the socks off of Ring. Also, with the app, you can move the view right, left, up, and down so I liked the functionality of the camera.

The camera does not replace an outdoor camera. It has to be plugged in so you will definitely need to use it somewhere indoors, which wasn't an issue for me since I already use Ring video camera outside. It would be nice if it had some temporary charge when not connected to power, but when the power is disconnected, the camera doesn't work.

I was able to connect to Alexa pretty easily. I had to enable a skill, which is key, prior to making it work. I was also able to connect it to Apple Home Kit very easily. I also use Google Home/Assistant, but after three attempts to connect it, I gave up. I will only use it with Alexa.

So, my opinion, is that it doesn't replace your outdoor camera, but the quality is great and is good if you are looking for an indoor option.

High Sierra Access II Laptop Backpack, Purple Smoke/Black, One Size This is a really nice backpack that hits the essentials but adds in a lot of nice side touches
Pros
the shoulder straps are easily adjustable with front pull down straps
* sternum strap, missing on too many other packs
* side compression straps, also missing on too many packs
* deep, tight mesh water bottle holders on each side (and if your bottle is tall enough the side compression stacks will keep it tight against the pack
* easy-to-grasp zipper pulls
* a small exterior carabiner on the front pocket
• loops for more gear/ties
• a small clip for keys on the interior

A host of varied pockets
•2 small soft-lined pockets (one vertical, one horizontal) center front suitable for a phone or similarly sized device
• in the first zipper area
• two large pockets nearly the width of the pack
• a smaller, narrow velcro-closed pocket
• an even smaller zipper-close pocket
• two pen holders
• 3 small narrow pockets (being the velcro and zipper pockets)

• The second zippered area is a large open area and a zippered pocket about 5" deep adn the wide of the

• The third zippered area has a padded laptop section (fits my 15" MacBook Pro comfortably} and a padded tablet area as well (fits my 9.5" iPad )

The shoulder straps are padded, wide, and comfortable
The handle strap is wide, padded, and feels robust (i.e. you can actually use it and do so comfortably)
the back is padded, mesh-vented, and comfortable
the bottom is reinforced/cushioned for the occasional thumping landing
the fabric is thick ripstop and water repellent (haven't tested) though should note that is not waterproof (very few backpacks are)
The whole bag itself is quite roomy

I've been holding off on replacing my fraying, duck-taped bag for a while now because I just haven' found anything that has the combination of features and cushioning that this beast has proved me for over a decade. But this one has me comfortable about finally passing the torch

Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam I selected this camera to mount on my front porch, with the intention of keeping a watchful eye on the front of the house. I was very skeptical of this camera because of the price and assumed that it would be a budget-grade solution as a result. It has proven to be better than I anticipated.

This is a single-camera solution with no dedicated monitoring station. It connects via the WiFi network and it can be monitored via phone which is handy when you’re away. It includes a power supply and all of the mounting equipment (minus the tools) to set it all up for outdoor use.

All of that sounds great, but as I write this the camera sells for under $40.

It has not performed like a $40 camera. It has been rock-solid so far – it’s stable, it has remained connected except for when I have had router issues, the image in the daytime is excellent and the night-vision mode is far and away better than I expected – I can read license plates on cars in the driveway at night.

This is not a complete security solution but rather is a single camera for zone security. There are more complete systems that offer more features and capabilities, but these cost a lot more and cover broader areas with multiple cameras. If you just need a single camera to monitor a fairly small area, and you have a wireless network to connect it to, this is a very affordable solution.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam

WiFi Video Projector, WEWATCH V10B Wireless Portable Movie Projector with Bluetooth Full HD 1080P Supported Home Theater Video Projector Compatible with HDMI, VGA, TV Stick, iPhone, Android The WEWATCH V30 Portable Projector is a good 1080p projector for its size. I watched some movies with the screen setup to 80-90 inches and the picture looked very good in a dark room. It's important to watch this projector in low ambient lighting due to its low ANSI lumens, as bright light will wash out the picture.

The size of the projector is not as small as the pictures make it seem. Though it is not advertised as a pico projector, I expected it to be smaller. With that said, the projector is not so large that it would be hard to transport or store when not in use.

Unfortunately, I was not able to get the Wi-Fi feature to work with my Iphone. This is not a dealbreaker for me, as I plugged a Roku stick into the HDMI port and the system worked well.

I was surprised by how good the native speakers sound. I found watching movies enjoyable and voices were easy to hear. There are adjustments for the bass and treble levels in the menus. The unit has a headphone jack in the rear which makes hooking up an external speaker set up a breeze.

The fan on the unit is very quiet and is not distracting while it is in use.

While I really like this projector, there is a large downside. The lack of keystone correction is a huge oversight. Placing this projector without keystone adjustment means the projector has to be directly in line with the viewing area making it necessary to use a tripod in most instances. Having to bring a tripod along, makes the unit less portable.

Overall, this is a small projector with a great picture, as long as you can place it in the perfect location without much ambient lighting. If WEWATCH added keystone correction and refined the mirroring feature, this would be a 5 star projector.
text_fidelity_b: WiFi Video Projector, WEWATCH V10B Wireless Portable Movie Projector with Bluetooth Full HD 1080P Supported Home Theater Video Projector Compatible with HDMI, VGA, TV Stick, iPhone, Android

Universal Smart Battery Charger Mark II For AA AAA C D 9V Li-on Ni-MH Ni-Cd Rechargeable Household Batteries With USB Charger Cell Port More than anyone, I really wanted alkaline charging to work like other rechargeable batteries but the sad reality is that they're just not made for it.

The reality of alkaline charging:
- Duracells seem to leak more than cheapo "Kirkland" brand from Costco.
- Energizers do not hold charge very well.
- All brands leak eventually.
- Takes a long time to charge.
- Unreliable even if successfully recharged -- usually, batteries are connected in series, which means that if one fails, the device will not work.
- Battery leak can happen while charging or while being used in the device, resulting in a very messy charger and messy device.

So after some dumpster diving (or at least, I raided the battery recycling bins at work), I came home with batteries of various brands. For a while, I really did use recharged alkaline batteries exclusively and kept my Ni-MH batteries in the drawer. What I found was that I needed to change the batteries a lot more often and I couldn't be sure that the battery would have a charge when I took it out of the drawer.

Leaking is a big problem. My charger now has one charging port that is stuck because the liquid got in to the spring mechanism and dried. I also have a couple of remotes and devices that had to be cleaned out because the batteries leaked.

In the end, I had to give up on the idea of recharging cheap alkaline batteries because of how long it takes to recharge and that it can leak at any time, potentially ruining your device (mostly, it's just oily and you need to clean it out with a tissue). I just couldn't trust those batteries.

So why did I still give this charger 5 stars? Although alkaline charging was a failed experiment for me, the charger is still a better-than-average Ni-MH battery charger. It has separate intelligent charging and LCD display for each battery and will trickle charge a battery even after the lights turn green. Other chargers that have the same features cost more -- and without the Alkaline charging capability. You really can't go wrong with this charger.
text_fidelity_b: Universal Smart Battery Charger Mark II For AA AAA C D 9V Li-on Ni-MH Ni-Cd Rechargeable Household Batteries With USB Charger Cell Port

text_fidelity_a:
Camera Armor Protective Case for Canon 40D/50D (Black) I liked the idea of getting a little added protection for my 40D and this case does protect it a little bit. However most of the protection is against simple scratches and abrasions for daily use. I was hoping for a little shock and water protection, which this case minimally provides.

The appearance is nice. It does add a little bulk to the camera but still allows you to handle all the controls. The rubber is grippy which makes holding it a little more secure but at the price that it also clings to any dust it comes in contact with. I do like the clear plastic protective screen. The lens cover seems a little pointless. The one use I have found for it, is to use to block out light when shooting through glass at zoos and aquariums, but even for that it is of limited value.

Pros
+ Good added protections from scrapes and scratches
+ Clear Plastic
+ Add's a Grippieness to the camera

Cons
- Gathers dust
- MSRP is rather high for the payoff
- Adds a little bulk

Summary:
This product is ok at protecting the aesthetics of your camera for resale for sure. I'm a little dubious about any shock protection during a drop, but I feel it is worth having installed. It does not get in the way of functionality. Probably not worth full MSRP, but does have value.
text_fidelity_b: Camera Armor Protective Case for Canon 40D/50D (Black)

Projector Portable 5G WiFi Video-Projector [2022 Upgraded] Movie Projector Mini projectors 5500:1Contrast 7500Lumen Compatible with Full HD 1080P iPhone,Android,FireStick,AV,VGA,HDMI,USB,TF ‎T5-White It's not always true you get what you pay for, but it's not a bad rule to live/shop by. And I'd say it perfectly describes this projector. It does a basic job and for what you pay, that's about what you should expect. No bells and whistles, not great quality, but "sufficient." It's up to you therefore to decide what perks/quality you want and how much you're willing to pay for it.

it is light, has a small footprint, has several means of connecting, all postives
it's a bit clunky to set for a height and some of the controls

Its clarity and brightness don't come close to matching my Epson (I often teach outdoors and can't use this projector as it's washed out in comparison), whether we're talking visibility or sharpness of text. That said, the Epson is 150-200 dollars more expensive. Is it worth it? I need that brightness and clarify for my purposes (showing lots of text) and settings (often outdoors). But if you are watching movies indoors in a relatively darkened room, then this will be adequate to that purpose and save you a good amount of money.

Sound is the same. Not as good as my Epson, and when we show movies in our driveway, I hook up external speakers, so I like better sound. But again, if that's not a big deal to you, it can suffice.

For the price, it's a decent value. I'd pay more for more, but that's a personal choice

Comfortable design, Right/Left Hand Use, Wireless, USB 2.0 with Nano transceiver for PC/Laptop/Desktop, works with for Mac/Windows Computers This mouse is fine, but nothing special. The small USB transceiver is nice. It's out of the way and won't catch on anything. The mouse itself tracks on just about anything and is very reliable. The battery compartment is easy to access, no hassle replacing the single battery. I comes with a brand name battery uninstalled which is very nice. No software to install these days, the old Vista machine recognizes it without issue.

However, it's too lightweight for my tastes. The “click” feels cheap to me and the scroll wheel is stiff. I have an older Logitech wireless mouse that has the larger USB transceiver and the batteries are a hassle to change, but it feels solid and works great. To be fair, this is a “Mobile Mouse”, so maybe lightweight should have been expected. I just didn't realize how much I would dislike the weight difference.

I won't send this Microsoft mouse back, but I wouldn't buy it again. I haven't had any problems with this mouse, it's just personal preference. I'll just use the Microsoft as a travel mouse. I suppose it's also possible that operation becomes smoother with use, but I'm in no hurry to use this mouse.

text_fidelity_a:
ARCTIC Breeze Pro USB Desktop Fan with 4-Port USB Hub This review covers two different models of the Arctic fan:

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>Model with USB hub:
I have been using the original ARCTIC Breeze for a while and have been very pleased with its performance, and especially pleased with how quiet it runs. The Pro model builds on that and adds a few more useful features.

Unlike the original model which had a bendable stem with a USB plug on the end, the Pro has a base so the fan can be positioned away from the USB port on the PC. The attached power cord is a little over 5 feet long, making it possible to put the fan on my desk and plug it into the PC on the floor.

The base also has 4 USB input ports, so it works as a USB hub. It has a 5V power input jack if you want to turn this into an active hub. The power adapter to do so is NOT included.

Unlike the single-speed original version, this has a knob so you can vary the speed. It's not precise, but there is a somewhat noticeable difference between low and high. It's a continually variable speed - you can turn the dial to whatever speed you like.

Best of all, it's just as quiet, if not quieter, than the original model. That's the biggest plus for me by far, since the cheap USB fans make a racket. This just makes a low-pitched hum. The build quality is solid - the base is sturdy, and the bendable arm holds its position well.

One negative: the packaging. It's in a clam shell package that is a major, major pain to open!

While it's more expensive than the original, the added benefits of being able to position it on a desk and use it as a hub makes the upgrade worth considering. Highly recommend.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>USA EDITION:
I've have (and use) a couple other Arctic USB fans and have been 100% satisfied with them. This new version (their "USA Edition") has a couple of improvements over past designs.

The base is a metal plate which increases the fan's stability when you're bending the stem to point the fan. The on/off/speed dial switch no longer has a lit LED ring around it. I never found the lit LED ring to be bothersome on the other Arctic fans, so having or not having it is not a big deal to me.

The base also does away with the USB hub connections that other models have. That's keeps the base more streamlined and allows it to have a lower profile. It also does away with the clam shell packaging, instead using a very easy to open box.

The build quality of this, like the other Arctic fans I have, is excellent. The stem is bendy by stays put where you want it; the operating sound is pretty hushed; the on/off/speed control works well. The overall design is attractive, with a red/white/blue color scheme and graphics.

It moves a surprising amount of air. No, it won't blow your hair back as a Vornado fan will, but this makes a noticeable difference in circulating air. The size makes it very easy to find a spot on your desk to position it.

While I can't speak to the long-term reliability of this as of yet, I expect it will last for some time. I have an Arctic fan similar to this that I've been using almost daily for the past 1+ years, and it still works as good as it did when new.

Looks good, works well, and easy to use. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: ARCTIC Breeze Pro USB Desktop Fan with 4-Port USB Hub

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk Sansa Fuze 4 GB Video MP3 Player (Black) This is my daughter's third MP3 player.
She wanted to try this one, since she loved the look of the design.
We figured how bad can a player be, right?
After seeing hers, my son ordered the same player.

Well, they do play music - for a while.
They also play videos nicely, albeit very small and hard to see.

As of today, with neither one a year old yet, one has had be to be sent back
to Sansa for work (totally locked up and could not even be rebooted). They took a
month to send back a refurb, rather than the one my son sent in with his music on it.

My daughter's lasted a little longer, but does freeze up often.
However, the latest trick is that it has part of the sound going out.
She had purchased four pairs of various headphones trying to get the sound to stop
cutting out, thinking it was the headphone's problem. Nope - turns out, it is the
player. Don't know what is wrong, but one of the stereo sides cuts in and out endlessly.

She'll be shopping for a new one, but it won't be this model anymore.
They are just too cheaply made to last. The technology has been around for a long time now,
and it shouldn't be that hard to make a decent, affordable player.
However, it seems like it might just be too hard for Sansa.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk Sansa Fuze 4 GB Video MP3 Player (Black)

Belkin 6-Outlet Surge Protector with 3-Foot Cord (Plus An Extra 6-Foot Extension Cord) I'm confused. I thought when I got this surge suppressor that the extension cord was meant to be used with it so you'd have a total of nine feet of cord if needed. Apparently, the extension cord doesn't actually fit the surge suppressor; the extension cord has three two-prong receptacles that you could plug, say, lamps and the like into, but you cannot plug the surge suppressor itself into it. The extension cord is clearly marked as being for two-wire polarized, as opposed to three-prong grounded, appliances. So that's more than a little misleading.

The surge suppressor looks heavy-duty, but you are cautioned in the packaging literature that it's not to be used with "sensitive equipment" like everything we use surge suppressors for: computers, TV, etc. You can't use it with things involving water, either, like aquariums. So what would I use it for? A blow dryer? I think not. To make it even worse, you are told to cover the receptacles on the extension cord if they are not in use. There are little plastic sliders that you're supposed to use for this purpose. But one of the sliders on the extension cord I received won't stay closed. China-cheap.

Belkin has some good products, but this one doesn't impress me very much. And the whole thing is packaged in one of those awful clamshells that you risk hurting yourself on when you take the scissors to it.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin 6-Outlet Surge Protector with 3-Foot Cord (Plus An Extra 6-Foot Extension Cord)

TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions This GPS is a real upgrade for me, but I still love my old one which is TomTom One. Too bad it's no longer supported by TomTom or I probably would not have chosen the TomTom Via 1525 to try out for review. The very first thing I noticed about it was that the screen was twice as large as on my One - a very coveted perk to me. I choose to still use separate GPS devices instead of my phone since my phone uses up data and the GPS doesn't, saving me $$.

I have only used the Via 1525 a couple of times and it worked perfectly. I had to make a new account to TomTom to update it and overall it took about an hour and a half. I had a couple of problems with the update and had to restart but it finally worked. It comes with a USB for charging from a computer and another to use in the auxiliary power port in the car, and a mounting disk to adhere to a good spot in the car. It's not as intuitive as I would like, but it's not hard to figure out and it took us straight to our destination both times. I purposely passed some streets it was telling to me turn on to just to see how fast it would recalculate a route and it recalculated quickly. It has a lot of options that are indicated on the product page, most of which I will probably not use.

It's too early yet to give it 5 stars, but definitely 4 for now. It's a GPS, it found satellites quickly, got me a route planned out and was easy to follow. What more do I want from it? I like it a lot. It's supposed to have lifetime traffic and lifetime maps.......or until TomTom stops supporting it too.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions

Shoulder Bag
Pros:
It is of great quality with sufficient padding throughout.

Cons:

Tripod
Pros:

text_fidelity_a:
Kidz Gear Wired Headphones for Kids - Ltd. Edition White Great headphones at a great price. These fit my little man very well, and they are so adjustable even I could put them on to check out the volume.

They seem very comfy - my picky kiddo puts them on haphazardly without doing careful adjustments and he never seems bothered by them. He really loves using them (and WOW how amazing for me to not go to bed with that one show's theme song stuck in my head all night).

I'm impressed by the sound quality, especially for this price.

My ONE complaint is that the sound limiter is a separate piece AND this is not clearly marked anywhere on the packaging. I used it for a few weeks before I knew the volume wasn't limited on his precious little ears, it was in an Amazon review that I found out I actually had to retrieve that from the spare part box and use it. I'd thought it was an adapter for other size jacks or soothing. There are no instructions or info booklets in the box, so if you give these as a gift, let the recipient know that volume limiter is separate. Since these are for kids, I don't understand why they don't just limit the volume on the headset itself. Or at the very least, find a way to plug it that holds more tenaciously (like a built-in tie from the headphone to the limiter). That tiny piece is fascinating for kids to remove and easy to lose.
text_fidelity_b: Kidz Gear Wired Headphones for Kids - Ltd. Edition White

text_fidelity_a:
Epson E11E221012 ProSense 307 GPS Multisport Watch with Heart Rate and EasyView Display - Black I work a lot with smart watches but this is the first health monitor/GPS watch I have used. I was excited to have the
opportunity to work with it, and I was hopeful that it would be a good unit. Epson is a brand I know well from their printers, so out of the gate I had some expectations. This watch has proven to be a mixed bag.

I will start with what I believe are the strongest features. This watch has a much better-than-average charger. Many watches I have used have a magnetic charger that is either poorly constructed or will not stay on the device it'’s charging. This one, however, is a clamp-based charger that does a good job of holding the watch even under its own weight without letting it slip or shift. I would have liked to see other manufacturers adopt this kind of charging clamp.

The battery lasts for a very long time. I charged it up completely and after taking it from the charger I deliberately left it on the shelf to drain. It's rated for 20 hours, and I assume that is for active use. Letting it sit idle, it lasted two weeks for me. It of course drains much faster when it is actively being used so once I started using it I had to charge it again. This is a handy data point if you're traveling - if you're going for a weekend, it holds enough charge to get through in most cases, and if you are an infrequent user it will retain a charge for a while.

The display is very clear and easy to read. I have had no issues at all with the display and I am very pleased with how easy on the eyes it is.

One of the issues I have with most wrist-wear of any kind is getting it to fit properly. I have large hands and wrists, and I found this watch to be a bit snug on even the loosest setting. This is par for the course for me. I was hopeful it would fit a bit better, but it wasn't to be.

The aggravation started when I set up the software and paired the watch to my phone. The Bluetooth pairing did not go smoothly and I tried several times to get it straight. I finally switched over to setting it up through the watch instead of through the phone, and I was able to get it working and connected. While this is an acceptable work-around for someone with patience, it is an aggravation for someone who prefers things to just work the way they're supposed to.

I will say I am not especially impressed with the software app. I think it is a little too overly complex and counter-intuitive, but it does work and it has a lot of features. It does a good job of tracking progress.

So, aside from setup and fit, how does it work? It seems to work well. I am very familiar with sport GPS units so I assumed this one would work about the same, and it does. It acquires the satellites and uses those to report position back to the phone app so you can track yourself. This is useful when you want to see where you went and how far. The speed of acquisition of the satellites seems to be roughly the same as with my hand-held units. The heart rate monitor seems to be good and in measuring manually for comparison it appears to be accurate. The step feature is a good quick measurement and is sufficient to replace a dedicated pedometer.

Overall this is a decent health watch, but there's some room for improvement. It looks great, it works well and it's easy to read. It is hampered by less-than-idea setup and software, and it would be nice if it fit a little better.
text_fidelity_b: Epson E11E221012 ProSense 307 GPS Multisport Watch with Heart Rate and EasyView Display - Black

Did not have to re-enter the product key code as you here some have to do. It's only been two days but I am presently Happy and I have messed with and built computers for years being 61 years old. Keep in mind;  Hynix has been making Computer chips for years and is one of the largest Chip manufactures in the world, I used their OEM RAM for years and so did Dell/HP/Compac and others. My point is they are not New to this Industry, simply New to the SSD Market, but this is right up their alley and their first entry tests out toe to toe with the best of them in the SSD Market. Hope this helps out some of you. I will update should anything change.

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm Finepix F70EXR 10MP Super CCD Digital Camera with 10x Optical Dual Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7 inch LCD This is a high quality camera, but you must take time to read through the owner's manual to understand how to get the best pictures. You can just grab it and point and shoot using it while in the "automode" setting, but the resulting pictures may leave you a little disappointed depending upon the photographic conditions. To get the highest quality photos you must become familiar with how this little beauty works. Unfortunately, you might have to print out and tote the manual with you when you find yourself in situations where your pictures aren't what you'd like, or you can't figure out how to do certain things like know what's behind the flashing icon error message, or how to simulate different types of film, or can you choose between clarity, reduced noise and dynamic range? This is not really a simple "point and shoot" camera and all images will turn out great. You will have to study it, practice with it, and most of all have patience and you will be pleasantly rewarded for your efforts. Though the indicators vary with camera settings, there are 23 different indicators just for shooting mode, and 12 for playback mode, not to mention the date/time stamp, battery level, and indicator. It can get confusing.

Although a basic manual booklet is included with the camera, a much more detailed manual must be uploaded from the enclosed CD and then all 125 pages can be printed out or read from your computer monitor. The manual covers all the material in the booklet almost page for page but includes much more information about features the booklet leaves out and the booklet will refer you to specific pages in the manual for more information. Also, in the manual are about 50 FAQ's that are very useful. I am a manual reader, (having written many technical SOP's) and appreciate having well-written and well thought out manuals that are understandable and succinct. Though I would have preferred a manual that I don't have to upload to my computer, it is well-written and many useful pictures are included.

This camera is loaded with many different options/features but accessing and understanding many of them will require reading the manual. For people who don't want to be bothered with all the bells and whistles this camera may be more than they need. I can see very serious photographers using this camera. Reading through the manual I have compiled a list of some of the various modes, options and features available:

Digital Zoom
Movie Mode
Silent Mode
Variable ISO settings
Image size selection
Aspect Ratio selection
Intelligent Face detection
Scene Position
Shooting Modes
EXR Mode
Film simulation
Dynamic Range
White Balance
Continuous Photography
Photometry - multi, spot, average

Playback Options:
Erase
Slide Show
Red-eye Removal
Image Rotation
Protection from accidental deletion
Crop
Resize
Voice Memo
Print Order
Time Difference
Format

Pages 37, 67-68, 86-87, 97-103, and 104-107 would be good to print out and keep with your camera as they contain tables of various camera functions and a trouble shooting chart.

I have taken many pictures and movies inside and out, light and dark, with this camera set on various settings. And though I have practiced with it now for several weeks, I still need to often refer to the manual when I choose to vary from automode. Some things I have found especially desirable are:

Silent Mode - I attend classical music concerts where flash photography is prohibited. This mode will silence all beeps and flashes.

Large viewing screen on the back of the camera. It is exactly 5.5cm x 4.0 cm.

Digital Zoom - extremely good. I attended a local minor-league baseball game and sat far away on the grass well beyond the playing field. I was able to fully zoom and still get good, clear, close-up shots of the players with no blurring.

Movie Mode - Completely surpasses any other I've experienced so far. Images are clear, colorful and the sound quality is excellent. Camera noise was heard and recorded while using the "zoom" function in Movie Mode though it was not very loud.

Multi-frame play back function is very useful to quickly scan for a particular picture.

Fine Pix Viewer Program was very easy to install on my computer. I use Windows XP.

Very good photography in low-light conditions.

Also some things I did not find particularly desirable but are not major flaws:

I cannot directly burn a CD using the Fine Pix Viewer Program which comes with this camera. I have to use another camera program, import the pictures into it and then burn a CD.

Very easy to accidentally turn it on or off and easy to get misfires.

The zoom lever is too sensitive. I have learned with practice to barely move it very slowly.

The camera does not give helpful suggestions on how to get a better picture as does my HP R717.

Not HD capable.

The higher the ISO the grainier the picture though a higher ISO is desirable when shooting in dim/low light levels. I have set the ISO level to 200 and that seems to produce the best pictures so far.

Almost too many options, modes and functions to choose from. Though you can immediately begin to take pictures using Automode, it will take time to fully understand the many other aspects and features this camera has.

In Summary:

I can find no major complaint concerning this camera. It takes excellent clear and colorful photos even in situations where I least expect it - indoors with no flash. Any poor quality pictures I have taken are not the fault of the camera but due to the photographer's ignorance of how to use/understand properly the many features of the camera. The basic mechanics of such things as battery and memory card installation are very easy. Battery charging is a very simple process and battery life seems long. The manual is detailed and covers more than I would probably care to know. This is almost more camera than I need, though I will continue to use it and will update this review as necessary.

UPDATE 2.9.15 - Been using this camera all these years and now it's beginning to show it's age and giving me some problems. The viewing screen on the back has a vertical big black bar but it doesn't appear on the actual pictures. And the lens cover doesn't always completely open when the camera is turned on. I still use it but it might be time to think about a replacement. It's been good though so I really don't have any complaints.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Finepix F70EXR 10MP Super CCD Digital Camera with 10x Optical Dual Image Stabilized Zoom and 2.7 inch LCD

text_fidelity_a: SENNHEISER HD 559 Open Back Headphone - Black Unlike the Sennheiser HD 598 headphones I often use, the HD 559 does not include a 3.5mm adapter plug, so if you need one, have it or you will be unhappy should you want to use these for a laptop or other small device.  To test these, I kept my adapter in the laptop and switched between the two headphones, listening to an assortment of various tracks so I could really compare the audio elements and physical feel of the headphones.  I prefer the HD 598 headphones over this newer model and see that they are both comparable prices now because a newer model is available of the 598's.  You may prefer the HD 559's if you prefer a tinner, bass accentuated audio, but I would rather hear the differentiation between the elements of audio which I hear more clearly with the HD 598's.  The separation is simply more refined and I guess I'm spoiled. The newer 559 is cheaper than the upgraded higher end model, and i find them to be a tighter fit which becomes uncomfortable and irritating when worn for hours at a time, something that I never experienced with the others.  I think this band is stiffer, too. These produce a much less elegant sound which some may prefer, but the more I listen to these, the more I wonder if there is something wrong with them due to the pounding sound which is replicated each time I switch to them.  To avoid prejudice, I had an assistant do the switching for me as I kept my eyes closed through several songs and an audio narration.  I worked in the film and video industry and always used Sennheiser earphones, so my experience with the brand spans decades. These just don't match up, and that may just be the cause of my disappointment. They are not bad headphones, they are not great for my desires in experiencing audio in either recording or playback modes.  Of note is that the detachable long cable is nowhere near as easy to remove or insert as my other headphones which is of concern.  This set was made in China and it comes in a no frills 2 part box with a simple document written in numerous languages.
text_fidelity_b: SENNHEISER HD 559 Open Back Headphone - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Bose Conversation Enhancing Headphones Black (770341-0010) I’m 40 and have high frequency hearing loss. I hear almost nothing from 1kHz & up in my right ear and 4kHz and up in my left ear. I only experience issues in loud environments(restaurants, etc) or when there is a lot of background noise, but I recently started experiencing low frequency tinnitus that was irritating so I started looking for solutions. I went to see an ENT doctor and went through the motions only for him to confirm that I have poor hearing for my age and it’s up to me if I want some expensive hearing aids. No way I’m dropping 5k... I began by just looking for something to relieve the tinnitus and ran across many people saying that noise canceling headphones helped. I then went to the Bose website and low and behold they had the Hearphones which also had noise canceling. I started reading reviews then first then I stopped by the store with my kids and tried them out. My son was across the store and I could hear him talking to his sister. I could also hear every word of the conversation of people not far away. I removed the Hearphones and could not hear my kids or the people talking. I did this a few times... tuning in on people, music, etc then removing the buds. Tried the noise canceling and the rumbling in my ears was almost gone. Needless to say, I was impressed. I discussed the warranty with the salesman...30 day return, 90 exchange for something else, & 1 year free replacement(btw the 1 yr starts replacement over every time you replace them). I was sold. I purchased them with the intention of using for 30 days and returning if I could do without them.

I have now had them for 1 month. Here is my experience... at first I hated the neckband and was considering returning, but I got used to it and now don’t notice it. I use them for 1 hour workouts every morning, driving in the car for phone calls, music, podcasts, noise canceling at work, so pretty much all day. The neckband twists a little while working out or running and you need to shift it back in place, but it’s not a big deal for me. I would prefer the Soundsport Frees for working out, but I can’t bring myself to spend another $200 for headphones when these are $500. The noise canceling is fantastic for the gym & office and allows me to listen to music at a much lower level, which saves what I have left of my hearing in the long run. I used the soundsport wireless for 1 year before getting these and the sound quality of the hearphones is better, plus the noise canceling, and it has the music boost/phone call boost. I gave my soundsports to my wife and now use these exclusively.

Hearing:
When there is a lot of noise I can put them on and hear every word of a conversation that I would normally not hear or tune all the noise out via the noise cancellation. I recently went to a concert and was shocked at how much I enjoyed the concert more while wearing them. I could hear the guitar strings, vocals, and so much more while having a conversation with my wife. Amazing! I even use them while listening to the stereo in my car because it sounds so much better. I am always surprised at the sounds that I miss while not wearing them.

Sound: Classic Bose sound. The best headphones I’ve owned and I’ve had a few nice sets including the Bose soundsports & Bowers & Wilkins. I enjoy music much more since having them.

Phone calls: Phone calls are so much better, I talk on the phone more now because I’m not struggling to hear the other person and I hear them in both ears.

Overall: They simply work great. One of the best features is the directivity. When you set it to front or focused it ignores the rear microphones. While at the same time merging the left & right sound together. You hear a little of the left in the right ear and vice verse which helps with conversations. If Bose can ever put this technology in earbuds like the Frees they probably could not keep them on the shelf. If you have hearing loss or tinnitus and love music buy the Hearphones. If you love music and have no hearing loss buy the QC30 or QC35 for the noise canceling feature.

There are other fun Easter eggs that I didn’t expect...Wearing these while listening to music creates a “karaoke” effect and you can adjust the world volume so that it increases your voice to blend with the music coming through the headphones. I also played my guitar and found that more enjoyable. I could hear the notes in more detail as well as hear my voice in more detail while playing. These are also great if you like to people watch. When you are in a mall or restaurant you can hear random people’s conversations from across the room in detail, while they think you are wearing headphones and not listening at all. If you have hearing loss and/or enjoy a premium set of headphones these are for you. I have not used any other hearing devices to compare, but there are plenty of other reviews that will provide that information.

My rating is 5 stars from my perspective, but here is the breakdown of positives and negatives as I see them:

Positives:
- The sound is amazing for music, podcasts, phone calls, everything. Probably the best sounding headphones next to the QC35
- Adjustable balance. I set the balance to about 20 toward my right ear and both ears feel equal again.
- The adjustable world volume is awesome. I constantly adjust when my surrounding are too loud or not loud enough.
- Treble/bass adjustment. I set the treble around 30 and my world comes to life.
- Noise canceling is superb. It has almost stopped my tinnitus altogether. Especially good in situations like moving the yard. Before the noise of the mower was exhausting , but now it does not bother me.
- Adjustable presets are nice
- The front, focus, & everywhere settings work great. I use the front 180 setting the most. The focus setting really boost voice in front of you which is very nice too.
- Hearing the outside world while listening to music is amazing. Especially when you want to hear music, but want to hear when someone talks to you.
- “Karaoke effect” is pretty cool and makes singing/playing more enjoyable.
Negatives:
- The neckband was annoying at first, but now I barely notice it.
- Sometimes the app does not connect right away, but it connects after a few seconds.
- You will get weird looks from people, but the look is them wandering if you are listening to them since you are wearing headphones. It disappears after you start taking to people.
- I worry about the durability of them sometimes, but with a free replacement of 1 year I feel better about that. Remember that if you swap them with the year the warranty starts over. I am considering the extended warranty they lasts 3 years.
- I don’t like the charge port, but the only thing to improve it would be wireless charging.
- You’ll get wind noise outside. Use the noise canceling.

Btw I bought these in the Bose store and wrote this review to help others with similar issues. The headphones have improved my life and I love using them for just about everything.
text_fidelity_b: Bose Conversation Enhancing Headphones Black (770341-0010)

The ERGO still worked but would occasionally get stuck when the support pegs would catch the pock and cause the ball to resist - not enough to really hurt anything but just enough to make digital drawing difficult and just enough to annoy me. This replacement ball has taken care of that for me and has proven to be a worthwhile expense for me.

The ERGO and the M570 have the same size ball, so this ball can be used in either (I was using the ball from my old M570 in the ERGO while I waited for this ball to arrive). Replacement is a 30-second procedure and requires no special tools, though a pencil does make getting the old ball out a lot easier.

There are two different finish types available, glossy and matte. I chose the glossy in red. Operation has been absolutely smooth with no resistance at all and no catches. I haven’t noticed any operational differences between it and the original gray ball that came in my ERGO. And, in my opinion, the dark red of this ball actually looks a little nicer than the original silver ball as well as the blue M570 ball.

This wasn’t an expensive replacement and so far it has worked out very well for me. It has restored operation of my trackball to what it was before I damaged the original ball, which is really all I needed. Based on my experience with it, this is an easy replacement ball to recommend if you need to replace the ball in either a Logitech M570 or an MX ERGO.

Garmin Forerunner 110 GPS-Enabled Unisex Sport Watch (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I did a lot of research before making this purchase. I'm training for my first half marathon and wanted something that could track my distance and time, as well as my heart rate...but at the same time I needed it to be very simple. This watch had great reviews across the board.
Each day you run the watch has to reset position (unless you just wear it throughout the day). Do not hit the GPS button until you are outside and clear of your home/building. A couple of times I tried to get a jump start on the watch and hit the button while getting ready inside. My run was off by nearly 200 feet. This may not seem like a lot but when you are running multiple miles it adds up.
As long as you hit the GPS button while outside though you won't have any problems. It was dead on every time when I did this.
The battery life lasts (depending on your distance) about four days with consistent use.
It recharges very quickly so if you run in the morning and at night, you will easily have a full charge prior to your second run...typically takes 3 hours or so for a full charge from completely dead.
Definitely recommend the watch, especially for beginner and intermediate runners.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Forerunner 110 GPS-Enabled Unisex Sport Watch (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Bang & Olufsen Beoplay H4 Wireless Headphones - Black First off, I admit to having a Bang and Olufsen love affair.
One look at the jaw-dropping phones they produced in the 80s and I was hooked.
Young and broke, I saved and finally got a used triangle phone. By the way, in the movie 'The Birdcage', the receptionist is using one of the Bang & Olufsen banana phones. B&Os are in a lot of films.
Why?

In my most humble opinion, Bang & Olufsen is at the top of the game when it comes to visual design. Over the years they have always shown products that are visually stunning, MOMA worthy.

This headset is no different.
It is true understated elegance.
The two shades of grey are exactly the 'right' shades. We all know what that means, it's like the difference between and on trend pleasing pink, and a Pepto-Bismol pink. The spun metallic is in a warm tone gives a more inviting feel to the set.
Easy to sync.
I do not expect these to sound like a $1,000 headset, if they were, I'd be slightly underwhelmed. But only slightly.
As far as dimension, the 3d effect, it's spectacular. The band or orchestra is right in front of you.
They pick up the nuance that other headphones miss. Funny story, I was listening to a song I've listened to a hundred times before, and heard some background that I had never heard before.

Just a heads up for those of us that wear red nail polish... I've taken these on and off so many times that little red streaks are starting to appear, as you can see in the photo. But you can also see how gorgeous these are.
text_fidelity_b: Bang & Olufsen Beoplay H4 Wireless Headphones - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combos, Cnacnoo Full Size Slim Keyboard 2.4GHz Silent Mouse with Nano USB Receiver Multimedia Keys for Windows, Laptop, PC, Notebook Free OTG Cable for Android Tablet Phone As an old, retired guy I spend a lot of time online gaming, streaming videos, and dabbling on social media. Over the last few months I've tried out a variety of keyboards and mice, some of them high end gaming gear. As soon as you take this keyboard and mouse out of the box it's clear that this is a low end rig. It just doesn't have the solid heft of more expensive equipment. That's not necessarily a bad thing though as I've used some excellent, inexpensive keyboards and mice. Sadly, this product is not of that caliber either.

The compact size makes the keyboard feel cramped when typing. Even as I'm writing this, my fingers are feeling strained from the cramped tightness. The manufacturer makes the 12 function/F key combos seem like a big deal. To me those combos just seem like an unnecessary complication. There are other, more standard ways of doing all those things without having to learn a whole new set of keys. The six "hot keys" seem to be just a set of video controls that duplicate functionality already available on any computer with a standard video player.

The mouse is particularly disappointing for anyone who does gaming. Now I'm just a casual gamer, by no means a hard core one, and even I find this mouse to be a handicap. In my main game you move your character forward by holding down both the left and right mouse buttons simultaneously. With other mice that is no big deal. With this mouse there is a perceptible hesitation or stutter before moving when holding down the buttons like that. That may not sound like a big deal to a non-gamer but that kind of stuttering can quickly get your character killed in a gaming battle. Also, it seems to take some effort to hold those buttons down. My fingers feel a strain in holding these mouse buttons down, a strain I haven't felt with other mice. And yes, I did try the suggested solutions for mouse problems offered in the "Manual" that came with this product (one tiny sheet printed on both sides). They didn't help.

So if you are mostly watching videos and reading Facebook on your computer, you will probably be okay with this gear. Any more serious use than that and you will want to pass on this stuff.
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combos, Cnacnoo Full Size Slim Keyboard 2.4GHz Silent Mouse with Nano USB Receiver Multimedia Keys for Windows, Laptop, PC, Notebook Free OTG Cable for Android Tablet Phone

text_fidelity_a:
SereneLife Battery Grass Cutter, Grass Clippers Cordless, Trimmer Cutter, Handheld Trimmer, Grass Shear Electric, Perfect for Leaves & Debris, Rechargeable Battery, Charge Time 4 Hrs, 3.6V Here are my thoughts about Roku. Generally I like the product, but in setting it up I had some concerns.

PROS:
**Easy to set up
**Compact - it's so small it fits in one hand.
**Picture quality is pretty sharp depending upon the source. It is not HD quality but more like a decent DVD (though not Blu-Ray).
**A number of free channels available through Roku. You can add a lot of content. Since I'm an old movie buff, I added Pub a Hub (public domain movies) and Crackle (pretty bad recent movies but some good classics, like Easy Rider).
**Picture is big. I have a friend who has a projector that's five times as big as the Roku, and yet the projected image is the same size. That's impressive.

CONS:
**How much radiation does this device emit? In the fine print, the instruction booklet reads: "This equipment complies with FCC radiation exposure limits set forth for an uncontrolled environment. This equipment should be installed and operated with minimum distance 20CM between the RADIATOR AND YOUR BODY."
Hmm. I don't know about you, but it's hard not to sit pretty close to the projector. I used it in the bedroom and watched a movie on the ceiling. Of course I had to be close to it in order to put it at the right angle. How much radiation is the device emitting?

**Roku asks for your credit card information before you can use the device. When you set up an account, even if you don't want anything other than the free channels, they force you to put your credit card on file. The other privacy issue I object to is the way Roku allows you to connect to Facebook. In order for Roku to work, you were pretty much forced to allow Roku to access your information on Facebook at any time (even when you're logged out!) Not happy about this.

**In order to add some channels to the Roku network, you have to establish separate accounts. That means establishing one for Netflix, one for Amazon, etc, if you don't already have one. This means I'm sharing my account information with a number of companies I may or may not want to do business with. No doubt all this information will be shared among the video providers. That means a lot of spam will be coming my way in my email.

**Roku is geared toward convincing you to subscribe to as many streaming (pay on demand) services as possible. I'm not sure I would pay $300 for it, as it is very much a device aimed to getting you to subscribe to streaming channels. You can use it other ways, but Roku feels like a product sponsored by many vendors, as opposed to a stand-alone projector.

My conclusion? I recommend it with some reservations as noted above.
text_fidelity_b: SereneLife Battery Grass Cutter, Grass Clippers Cordless, Trimmer Cutter, Handheld Trimmer, Grass Shear Electric, Perfect for Leaves & Debris, Rechargeable Battery, Charge Time 4 Hrs, 3.6V

iPad Stand TechMatte Multi-Angle Aluminum Holder for Tablets, E-Readers and Smartphones, Nintendo Switch - Mini Stand The heft of this stand is impressive. I was expecting a lightweight stand, but was really surprised at how heavy and solid it was when I took it out of the box. It's the type of stand that I get the impression that I could run over with my car and not damage it. The hinge and the "kick stand" portion are made of plastic, but they also feel substantial.

The angle is set by depressing a button in the hinge area. It's very easy to adjust, and the hinge has click stops at various angles that hold it securely.

What is not adjustable is the depth of the cutout that holds the tablet or phone. I didn't have any problems with it holding a variety of tablets (iPad, Kindle and Nexus). It won't, however, hold some tablets that have a skin on it. The cutout that holds the table is slanted, and is 10mm at the widest point at the top, and 8mm at the narrowest point at the bottom. You'll want to measure your tablet plus skin to make sure it fits.

The cutout for the tablet has a plastic non-skid insert that works well. The stand itself also has plastic nubs on the back to prevent scratches on the tablet, and nubs on the bottom to prevent scratches on the table top. The nubs also act as non-skid points.

Very solid build quality, very easy to adjust in a variety of angles, and the design ensures that there won't be any damage to the tablet when you take if off/put it on the stand. As long as the width does not present a problem, this is a great choice for a tablet stand. Highly recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Bluetooth Headphones Wireless Earbuds Sports Over-Ear Bluetooth 5.3 Ear Buds with Earhooks 120H Playtime Wireless Headphones for Workout Waterproof Audifonos Bluetooth inalambricos LED Power Display I find that the best price to performance is in the $30 range for Bluetooth headphones, and they keep getting better and better. I have several pairs that I use for the gym, general listening to music, watching movies, and playing poker. I like to have other charged ones ready to go if a pair gets low.

These were rated very well, so I decided to give them a shot. They are super comfortable and they stay in place at the gym. I am not an audiophile, but these are well balanced and have better sound quality than my other pairs.

The greatest thing about these is the battery life- I used them for about 11 hours, and there was still 50% battery life left. With all my other pairs the battery life is a real problem, and it does not improve as they age. The charging case is also nice and there is a display for remaining battery life of the case. Remaining battery life of the headphones is displayed on the mobile device.

The BT connection is also super reliable. I have not experienced any disconnects or interference.

There are a couple cons (no product is perfect) and I want to briefly discuss them.

1. The rubber snap-on ear buds are not universal. They have a unique oval shape where they snap on and are secured. I have a bunch of spares, but they will not fit on here. If you lose one or it breaks it is useless. It comes with 3 sizes, but most people are probably like me and can only use the one size that fits.

2. The gain is too high on these. Adjusting the volume from zero, there are not many steps until the volume is too high. This means that micro-adjustment of the volume is not possible. All my other pairs I can use at 100% volume or near this (though I would not recommend it) and there there are maybe 15 or more micro-adjustments all the way back down to zero. Also, the notifications "power on," "power off," and "connected" are too loud. It's possible that with different mobile phones they behave differently, and there may also be an adjustment for this.

In summary, I highly recommend these. They are comfortable, they stay in place, they stay connected to my device, and they sound great. Probably the biggest Pro is the battery life. I purchased these to use as a backup for my other pairs, but it turns out that these will be my main headphones.
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Headphones Wireless Earbuds Sports Over-Ear Bluetooth 5.3 Ear Buds with Earhooks 120H Playtime Wireless Headphones for Workout Waterproof Audifonos Bluetooth inalambricos LED Power Display

1. Easy to set up - I used my previous monitor video cable and power cord and had it up and running in a few minutes.

What could be better:

3. While testing the volume on this monitor you must still figure out how to toggle using the various buttons underneath. There is no single volume button or toggle switch. And it will not get very loud.
4. If you don't bump the monitor or use the toggle switches the monitor stays fairly steady on it's stand. Otherwise it will rock and jiggle while using the buttons.
5. No HDMI cable is included.

The scant instructions did say to visit their website to download the latest drivers but as of yet this monitor is not listed in their driver drop down window. I don't think that matter much at this time as the monitor is very clear and sharp.
Overall: Good monitor for the price (as of this review it costs $138.24 Prime) which I feel is a fair price.

text_fidelity_a:
Aileho Kids Waterproof Camera Best Pool Toy for Children Birthday Gifts 1080P Kid Digital Underwater Camcorder Sports Action Cam 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 Year Girls 32G SD Card (Dark Purple) [[VIDEOID:e832f455c8dfddb522ae3bbc1ec73698]] Loved the idea of an underwater camera for kids, and this one would have been great if not for the terrible image quality that would only disappoint any except maybe youngest of kids.

When I unpacked the box, I had great expectations. The waterproof shell seemed to be solid and to seal well, and there was a whole lot of extra parts to attach the camera to a bicycle and so on. Camera is very small, but the little screen is bright and it shows the image you're taking clearly. The interface is intuitive and reasonably simple. (I didn't bother to set the date before trying out the camera, but the instructions were clear, and I was able to test it with no problem, it works.)

HOWEVER: I can't believe how bad quality of the images are! They look jagged and pixelated like they're at 480 pixels. Even when I increased the quality in the settings to maximum image resolution, which is supposed to be 20Mb and 7344 pixels (more than what I shoot at for my professional photography biz), the quality stayed the same and the file size only crept up to just below 1 Meg. No idea how they managed to accomplish that. Their image sensor is at about the quality of those blurry, pixelated security cameras that are completely useless for identification. Otherwise, this camera focuses surprisingly well and handles a wide range of light conditions automatically. All the images were in a good range.

The video was marginally better, but still not what you'd expect at 1080 resolution. Camera was recognized by my Windows laptop right away, and I was able to access and copy images with no problem.

It's such a shame that the manufacturer decided to save money on image quality and it's a weird business decision that makes an otherwise fun and well built product useless.

Photos above were taken by the reviewed camera:
- The instruction manual image at highest resolution, and you can see its file size in the second screenshot image. Taken without the waterproof case.
- First Batman toy image at default resolution, without waterproof case
-Second Batman toy image at default resolution, with waterproof case on. Surprisingly, not much difference. Good plastic.
text_fidelity_b: Aileho Kids Waterproof Camera Best Pool Toy for Children Birthday Gifts 1080P Kid Digital Underwater Camcorder Sports Action Cam 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 Year Girls 32G SD Card (Dark Purple)

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive Fit (MUF-128BB/AM) I bought 2 of these, they came today, and I and am returning them both tomorrow.

Chief reason: the drive is so small, that it is hard to plug into either USB port in the back of my new TV, a Sony XBR 850C. That TV has a somewhat constricted space where all of its ports are (USB, HDMI, etc). I just learned the hard way that I really need a longer drive to easily insert/remove it with this TV. Anyone else in a similar situation should likewise give this drive a serious rethink. I note that I had little problem with inserting/removing this drive from the front of my workstation, where I have unrestricted space.

Secondary reason: this drive has poor write speeds. My first transfer was of a single 2 GB movie file--a pure sequential write, which should be optimal--and yet I got an initial speed that started at ~50 MB/s and then it decay to maybe 40 MB/s. I should have paid more careful attention to the write benchmarks of this drive. I really want >= 100 MB/s write speeds.

It looks like my best bet is this drive's bigger brother, the Samsung 32GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive MUF-32BA/AM. Ordering 2 right now, stay tuned...
text_fidelity_b: Samsung 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive Fit (MUF-128BB/AM)

text_fidelity_a:
Canon Powershot A1200 12.1 MP Digital Camera with 4x Optical Zoom (Silver) (OLD MODEL) OK, here are the facts: my other (similar) camera developed a glitch -- it will not allow me to delete photos without loooooong delays. So I went in search of an inexpensive replacement camera. I settled on this Canon.

I did so with trepidation because some of the reviews were lukewarm at best. Yet other reviewers loved it. (This, by the way, is what makes horse races!) So I thought I would take a chance.

Here is why I am happy with my choice: (1) the viewer seems larger than its dimensions suggest; (2) the camera fits in my shirt pocket; (3) the pics are crisp indoors and out; (4) the on-off button is clearly marked and the shot button is nice and robust. For me, these features are all I need. To be sure, the camera has a few video bells and whistles -- I'll try those one of these days. No rush.

A Con: the shot button takes a little getting used to, since it appears to have two stages to it. If you just press and disengage, nothing will happen. It requires a little patience and then it will take the picture. I can live with that idiosyncrasy.

Another Con: no internal memory. You must purchase an SD card before you can use the camera. This too I have accepted, because having pics on cards does make it easy to load them into PCs and laptops.

If you are looking for a simple "point-and-shoot" camera that will also perform other tricks if you are of a mind, go for it!
text_fidelity_b: Canon Powershot A1200 12.1 MP Digital Camera with 4x Optical Zoom (Silver) (OLD MODEL)

text_fidelity_a:
12x42 Binoculars for Adults - HD Low Light Night Vision - Compact Lightweight (1.05lb) - Powerful BAK4 Prism FMC Lens - Waterproof Binoculars for Bird Watching, Hunting, Sports -Phone Adapter Included In this $30-50 price range, I think you should stick with this one. We got another one listed at $40 and besides for the branding, it seems to be the same binocular with slight molding differences. The tech is the same. Don't bother spending a little more unless you really want to upgrade and get one with zoom function. All these economy versions do not have zoom. And if you're new to binoculars, there is a learning curve, but this is how you focus:

1. Set the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial to ZERO and set sight on a distant subject. I'm not sure what zero means since there are no numbers, but there are arrows, so I presume it's when the arrows line up.

2. Cover the RIGHT FRONT lens with your hand, and rotate the FOCUSING WHEEL (the middle wheel), until the image is sharp. Keep both eyes open while you make this adjustment.

3. Now cover the LEFT FRONT lens and rotate the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial until the image is sharp. So here, you're not touching the focusing wheel, you're adjusting the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial.
text_fidelity_b: 12x42 Binoculars for Adults - HD Low Light Night Vision - Compact Lightweight (1.05lb) - Powerful BAK4 Prism FMC Lens - Waterproof Binoculars for Bird Watching, Hunting, Sports -Phone Adapter Included

text_fidelity_a:
Philips - Hue Play Starter Kit - Black First effort at setup was very frustrating, so I waited a day and started over.

The lights are powerful and intelligently designed. I did not buy them for the tv reason other people do. I just wanted a colorful backdrop for my FaceTime calls. In setting these up, I ended up crippling a few of my lights in a way that they now only offer about 9 colors, which is a problem I'll have to fix.

I agree with others, the cords to these a). shouldn't be proprietary, and b) shouldn't be black. They should be white to blend in with a wall. So I'll be buying a skinny extension cord to make up for that. Maybe they can change that for future customers.

The fact that the lights must both be plugged in to the same source is a definite buzzkill. And like everyone else who loves Hue, I have about 20 lights in my small place.

Once set up, I liked them a lot. They do all the colors and are fairly flexible with Alexa on the dimming, even more so on the app. But I don't recommend putting the app on the same network as your computer, these lights are VERY easy to hack, and if they do get hacked, they can get into your computer. The FBI warned against all iot (internet of things) devices like this.
text_fidelity_b: Philips - Hue Play Starter Kit - Black

Belkin UltraHD Premium HDMI Cable (2 Meters / 6.6 Feet) This is a very nice, basic cable.

I am surprised that the description does not mention Ethernet support. That concerned me, as it just looks neater having one cable in place of two. However, the cable is printed that it does support Ethernet, and testing it, this is the case. I plugged one end into a receiver that has an Internet connection, the other end into a Raspberry Pi that has no WiFi dongle and it was able to download a file from my DropBox account. I suppose that's such a standard feature, it's not worth mentioning anymore.

The cable seems sturdy enough, but I almost never put my cables through hard use. I set them up and leave them alone. The ends are stiff against bending, which means added support for the most fragile connection. It's reasonably thick, doesn't seem prone to tangling, and does exactly what it should. I am pleased with it.

text_fidelity_a:
VELCRO Brand ONE-WRAP Cable Ties, 100Pk, 8 x 1/2" Black Cord Organization Straps, Thin Pre-Cut Design, Wire Management for Organizing Home, Office and Data Centers I use these exclusively for cable management - I pass the end of the strap through the slot so that the strap is permanently secured to the cable, then bundle the cord up. EZPZ. Great value for the money, I bought two bags to organize my cables and I should probably be set for the next twenty years or so. Much better than constantly scavenging velcro straps from new purchases. I prefer these to wire ties, as they can be secured to the cable, stick better, apply force over a broader area and look a far bit more orderly when properly installed.

The straps are of good quality, adhere very well, and are easy to remove when you want to. The length is suited for wrapping up, say, most of your average 10-15ft computer or AV cables, it hasn't been a problem yet.

Only annoying thing is that when the factory punched out the slots in the strap, it only did so partially, so the little central bit is still stuck to the velcro most of the time. Bothersome, but not excessive so, you just have to tear it off each time. Another nitpick would be that I prefer my straps to have a constant width, rather than tapering down near the end - again, looks neater IHMO.

Other than that, would recommend.
text_fidelity_b: VELCRO Brand ONE-WRAP Cable Ties, 100Pk, 8 x 1/2" Black Cord Organization Straps, Thin Pre-Cut Design, Wire Management for Organizing Home, Office and Data Centers

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First, let me preface that I in NO way count myself a photog. I am just a shutter bug who has been firing frames almost non-stop since the age of 18. I learned on my dad's 'old' Nikon SLR with an f/1.2 lens. The Nikon SLRs/DSLRs I have owned are: N50, N60, N55, N80 and D50. My N50 ad N80 had the best lenses. The N60 and N55 were not as great and the D50 was a fabulous entry-level digital. The only medium format camera I own is my Holga. But hey, unlike the photographer at Portrait Innovations, at least I know 'medium format' does not refer to the number of megapixels at which I am shooting. As for my working knowledge, I had three semesters of photography in college. I can process/print both B&W and color film. (Not that that does me any good these days LOL) I can shoot completely 'manual' and I have stood among many pro photographers on the bridge at sunset, waiting for the color to be just right on Half Dome. (My Bogen tripod was way too heavy to be practical for an amateur but it gave me street credit.) So, in a nut shell, I shoot by the 'Sunny 16' rule. I know that opening my f-stop should increase my shutter speed give me a shorter depth of field; and, per the great Ansel Adams, f/8 is a proper exposure for all pictures.

That said, I hate my D3100.

I have had metering issues since I opened the box. I bought the camera so I could take 'even better' pictures of my infant son than I was getting from my D50. Ha. Joke was on me.

The contrast was BLINDING on the factory settings and every shot was over exposed. I have tried every metering option in the menu but the only changes I can achieve are under-exposure, blurred focus and missed shots. It's go high or go without.

I always lower my ISO to 100 when I'm outside because I crave rich color but it's just not there. I have tried Aperture Priority, Shutter Priority and Manual. Nothing. f/16 over my film speed on a sunny day. That's supposed to work! I have used it on many a 'less complicated' camera and achieved photos that make jaws drop. Well, there's no jaw dropping with this camera.

The metering overrides my manual choices every time. It's like I'm having a battle of wits with my camera. :( It reminds me of the days when Kodak was marketing 800-speed film as a universal, never-miss-a-shot solution to all your photo woes. Bleh. Just because there's always an image doesn't mean it's the RIGHT exposure.

I get that being an entry-level/made-for-the-masses DSLR really does mean it's a glorified point-and-shoot but it should preform at least as well as it's predecessors. Honestly, I got far more reliable results from my Canon SureShot and a roll of Kodak 100.

My expectation for a camera is that the image should be very close to perfect when the shutter closes. I know there's always room for improvement before printing but that's the art of photography. The hours I spend working on my photos after the shot should be to make them pop. Instead, my time is spent trying to rescue precious memories.

If you are considering this camera as your first DSLR because you think it will improve your skills, skip it. Invest in an equally expensive point-and-shoot that will give you all the same manual controls and preform much better in low-light situations. The D3100 does not live up to the standards of a Nikon SLR.

I gave it a second star because my son pulled mine off the counter about a year after I bought it and although the case cracked, it didn't seem to hurt the camera. Unfortunately, it impact didn't help it, either. (Yes, I was actually hopeful.)
text_fidelity_b: Nikon D3100 DSLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6 Auto Focus-S Nikkor Zoom Lens (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

OTTERBOX SYMMETRY FOLIO SERIES Case for Microsoft Surface Pro 7 - Retail Packaging - STARRY NIGHT (CLEAR/BLACK/BLACK PU/DARK GREY MICROSUED) I ordered this OtterBox Symmetry Folio Series Case for use as my wife has a Surface Pro 7. The Pros and Cons are listed below:

Pros:
* The case fits the surface tablet quite snugly
* The back is clear, which allows you to showcase the Surface Pro 7's sleek encasement
* It has a fold-able cover that can be manipulated into a stand for the Surface when using it like a tablet
* The case's sides are made of a thick rubber that would provide some protection for the corners of your Surface
* The case base would provide decent protection

Con's:
* You can not use the case with the attachable Surface Keyboard, so you are limited in using your Surface only as a
tablet.
* The clear back scratches and marks easily. giving it a worn and unclear view of the back of your surface.
* The fold-able cover is not very good protection for your screen, it is relatively thin
* Because the cover is relatively thin, it is not really a stable stand when folded and the tablet is on it

This case does not really live up to the OtterBox brand. It seems quite an inconvenience to not be able to use your Surface keyboard without taking the case off. You would be limited in only being able to use your Surface as a Tablet. For some this maybe acceptable. But for my wife who travels extensively and uses her Surface more than her desktop for work, that just is not feasible. Plus, having to buy additional protection for your screen is also a negative aspect. I just would not trust this cover alone to keep the screen safe from breakage.

Overall, my wife will not be using this case on her Surface.
