text_fidelity_a:
Michael Kors Lexington 2 Smartwatch - Black Stainless Steel If you like fully featured smart watches, it is hard to find anything this watch can't do! It runs Google's Wear OS, which is their watch variation of Android, so Google users should feel right at home with it. It's got a Play Store for apps, a really fluid interface, and of course it integrates really well with an Android Smartphone. I've been told it doesn't play as nicely with iPhones, but a lot of the core features are standardized and cross platform so it can still function as a really nice watch and allow notifications and call support regardless of device.
My wife had a Fossil Wear OS watch previously, and the feature set is very similar except for one huge plus this has: A SPEAKER! Many of the third party entry level Wear OS watches have a microphone for digital assistant commands and voice-to-text typing, but lack a speaker for it to talk back. So you have to read your responses on the screen and you can't exactly take phone calls. But THIS ONE DOES! Thanks to the speaker, you can full on take calls like a modern day Dick Tracy. That's really useful and cool, especially if you put your phone down or have it in a pocket you don't want to pull it out of all the time.
But here's the big con:
BATTERY LIFE. While this is better than other wear OS watches I've tried, it seems like Wear OS is so feature-filled, they generally need to be charged as often as smartphones do. Battery obviously depends on usage, but average use seems to last about a day or two at a time. Heavy usage and you'll need to top it off every night at least. This isn't the fault of this watch, but rather Wear OS in general. Other smart watches such as the Samsungs and FitBits can go for days to nearly a week on a charge, which means you not only won't have to worry about charging it more than once or twice a week, but you also can do sleep tracking and just leave it on at night. That's something I'm trying to do in order to have healthier sleeping habits. Some devices such as the Mi Band and Amazefit can go for around 20 days on a charge! I was using a Mi Band 3 before trying this watch, and while it doesn't run apps or have a full color screen or take phone calls, I think I prefer having a watch that only needs to be charged about once a month, and can show me my sleeping data as well as pedometer and activity charts, all while alerting me to notifications. I feel like Wear OS has a ways to go before I'm ready to switch over full time. The good news is that devices ARE getting better, as this shows. If you love Wear OS and the smartest features available, this is a good option. But personally I think I'm going back to my "smartwatch lite" that has less bells and whistles but actually fits better functionally into my life.
I want to give this 3.5 stars, I feel like 3 is too low because it IS good for what it is, but I also don't like it enough to use it daily. So settling on 4.
text_fidelity_b: Michael Kors Lexington 2 Smartwatch - Black Stainless Steel

Aluminum Laptop Stand, tomtoc Foldable Notebook Stand with Adjustable Eye-Level Ergonomic Design, Portable Laptop Holder for MacBook Air Pro, Dell XPS, Surface Laptop and More 11 to 15.6 Inch Laptop I know, you are probably thinking- what kind of idiot would try this on their LAP? I can not tell you who, but let's just say I am a witness.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This little stand folds perfectly flat. It comes in a drawstring bag which keeps it from attacking you. You see, this is VERY easy to pinch your fingers in. I have the bruises to prove it. However, once I figured it out, I was able to avoid it any more. Keeping this in the case is a GOOD thing.

HOW TO USE THIS
When I first got this, I was explaining to a certain someone that this was to keep the laptop cooler and hold it at a better angle. It was not until that certain someone was carrying on about what a stupid device it was that I realized that this someone was trying to use it on their lap. Don't do that. You won't like it.

HOW DOES IT PERFORM?
There are silicone pads and 3 settings for this stand. The pads hold the laptop in place and the stand in each setting. It holds a lightweight laptop well and the angles are good. I found using it on the right table top helps. It seems to stay put well, but if you have a really slick top, you can always put a non-skid pad under the whole thing.

THE BOTTOM LINE
As long as you are careful and only use this on the table top and are careful about not pinching your fingers, this is a nice little stand. It holds pretty well and is at a decent angle so far for our lightweight laptop.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. It is hard to use unless you really pay attention because it can suddenly fold down pinching the fingers, so I took a star off for that. It is a nice stand so far, but I will update as we try other laptops on it over time if necessary to let you know if something changes.
text_fidelity_b: Aluminum Laptop Stand, tomtoc Foldable Notebook Stand with Adjustable Eye-Level Ergonomic Design, Portable Laptop Holder for MacBook Air Pro, Dell XPS, Surface Laptop and More 11 to 15.6 Inch Laptop

text_fidelity_a:
BUGANI Bluetooth Speakers, M83 Speaker IPX6 Waterproof Portable LargeWireless Speaker,Bluetooth 5.2, Wireless Two Pairing,24H Playtime,Suitable for Family Gatherings and Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker I ordered this for the higher wattage and on my primary phone, it does get quite loud; but on my Dex device, it's maxed out is equivalent to about 50% volume on a 10W speaker.
I used a dB meter that was about 6ft away with the speaker pointed towards the meter. At max volume on my main phone (fold3) and at 150% volume, I was getting a consistent mid-90s dB for melody and lyrics, with peaks up to 109dB. On my other device (Note 10+), also at 150%, it was pulling about 70 dB on TV dialogue. I did try testing it with a volume booster, and even with only 110% (on top of the 150%) it was beginning to distort.
I played the TV audio for about 16hrs at moderate and 8hrs on low, and it was reading as still having 70% battery. But after only a few hours of moderate-high volume music, that 70% was gone and it died.
The sound quality is quite good with a warm tone. The highs are clear and the bass is better than I expected for there not to be a dedicated bass cone.
Despite appearances, I think the best use for this will be background music - not too loud will keep it playing all day & night and it will provide a much cleaner and richer sound than a small speaker at similar volume.
text_fidelity_b: BUGANI Bluetooth Speakers, M83 Speaker IPX6 Waterproof Portable LargeWireless Speaker,Bluetooth 5.2, Wireless Two Pairing,24H Playtime,Suitable for Family Gatherings and Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker

text_fidelity_a:
Moshi iVisor XT (HD clear) No-Bubble Screen Protector for the Fire HDX 8.9" I purchased this protector due to the overwhelming positive reports from other verified buyers. I do not like my cell phone's screen being unprotected and now with my first Kindle I feel the same way. The HDX screen is gorgeous and I want a way to keep it as such. This screen protector seemed the answer to my predicament.

This protector is, indeed, extremely simple to 'install'. It takes more time to remove it from its packaging and throw the trash away afterwards than it does to apply the protector itself. Simply line up the cutouts on the protector film with the camera and flash at the top and center of your Kindle and you are done. I found it helpful to guide the film into place by kind of rolling the sides down, guiding them to ensure proper placement. Then just apply a little pressure (basically, run your hand around the edges) to activate the adhesive.

Only the outer black margin of the protector has adhesive to stick it to the border and outer edges of your Kindle, thus leaving the clear center which covers your Kindle's screen loose, or non-sticky. This manufacturing and design approach has both pros and one con I have noticed so far.

Pros:

It allows for lightning fast and super easy installation.

Because of the solid black border, you can accidentally touch the sticky side while installing and lining it up without any fingerprints showing through as with a normal screen protector. This was a bonus to me as these things are always so difficult to install without this happening.

The clear center portion that covers the screen is completely 100% bubble free.

Due to some micro hairs/fibers being on the screen despite having wiped it down prior to installing the protector, I learned that I could remove the protector (lifted up one corner and peeled it halfway back to do a quick swipe with the MF cloth again) and it would re-adhere to the Kindle's surface just as well as it did the first time.

The company claims that, if it should lose its stickiness, the protector can be rinsed/washed and used again. I have yet to need to go this far so I cannot comment on the credit-worthiness of this claim, however from my experiences so far, I can see the possibility of this claim holding up.

I have not noticed any blurring or the rainbow affect the company mentions on its packaging. The screen is crystal clear and appears to not even have a screen protector on it.

Con:

Since the clear center portion does not adhere to the screen, it is allowed to float just above the screen thus reducing the screen sensitivity and requiring more force from either your fingertip or your stylus.

After using my Kindle for a few hours after installation of this screen protector, I have come to the above conclusions. As bad as the con is for me and my preferences, I will leave it on for a few days to give myself a little more time and to see if anything changes. This screen protector ranks very high on my list of desirable protectors (I even searched to see if they make a version for my Droid cell phone) so I am really hoping that the sensitivity issue works itself out soon.
text_fidelity_b: Moshi iVisor XT (HD clear) No-Bubble Screen Protector for the Fire HDX 8.9"

Belkin N150 Wireless USB Adapter with up to 150Mbps Link Rate We have several networked devices in our house and also several individualized networks configured. Not all of the networks can be seen by all devices so I looked to this Belkin USB WiFi adapter to allow one of the older computer systems to access the most reliable network in the house - a 5GHz network that only one or two of the systems can see.

Installation was a snap. I popped in the CD, told it to install the drivers and we were off to the races. The particular target system was a 32-bit Windows Vista laptop. After just a couple of minutes the driver was completely installed and when I plugged in the USB adapter is was picked up immediately. I could see the desired network as well as several other networks in the neighborhood that were previously invisible to the computer. I shut off the built-in adapter, connected to the 5GHz network and went to the net.

So far, the connection has been very stable and speeds have been excellent. The router to which it is connected is a TP-Link router and so far we have seen no issues between the two devices. I have not had this adapter very long so it is still early to say it’s completely stable but all indicators up to this point have been very favorable.

Several other reviewers have mentioned that this adapter does not work with Linux. This is true - there are no drivers available for this adapter other than for Windows XP/Vista/7/8. If you need an adapter that will allow you to connect a Linux or Mac system to a wireless network, this is not the device you need right now.

So far I can’t find too much about which to complain concerning this router. It seems to be stable and reliable on the system to which it is attached here. I am satisfied with it and based on my experience with it can recommend it - if you’re sticking with Windows.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin N150 Wireless USB Adapter with up to 150Mbps Link Rate

Mohu Sky 60 TV Antenna, Outdoor, Amplified, 75 Mile Range, Durable Lightweight, Mount Kit Included, Roof or Attic, 4K-Ready, 30 Foot Detachable Cable, Premium Materials for Performance, MH-110585,Black REVISED to 4 Star review: After using the antenna a week, I re-ran the channel search--which I should have done after installing it. I am able to pick up 38 of the 45 channels within a 60 mile radius of my house. They all come in very clearly. The amplifier wasn't working at all, and we determined that the brick was defective. Plugging it into another USB brick didn't really improve the signal by much, but it at least worked.

All-in-all, I'm glad I bought it. I'm able to clearly receive: 4 PBS stations; 3 CBS stations; 1 each NBC and ABC; plus FOX, CW, and an assortment of crap (TCT, HSN, QVC) networks. Enough to make me happy to leave TWC and in the dust.

UPDATE: 8/2/2016 What I have found is that the signals from channels with transmitters within 10 miles are not being up, while those 12 miles and beyond are coming in clearly. I suspect this is due to my location and not the antenna. Still, the amplifier causes the entire thing to not work, so I don't know what's up with that thing.

This antenna arrived as indicated. However, instead of the nearly 45 channels within a 60 mile radius of my home, I'm only able to get about 15. I installed it on the roof, and the direction did not seem to make a difference. NOTES:

Originally, I hooked this up and leaned it against the back of the TV before I had someone install it. I got no more channels installing it on the roof than I did that way.

The amplifier which comes in the box with this antenna actually made the signal worse--not better, so I disconnected that.

Give the few number of channels that actually come through, on hindsight, I would have bought a much cheaper antenna. It does not pull in channels more than about 20 miles away. Even channels 20 miles away aren't received.

Otherwise, the reception on the channels that do come through is great.

All of this may be because I am in an old, downtown neighborhood, with close houses and lots of trees. Although I installed it in an area of the roof free of trees.
text_fidelity_b: Mohu Sky 60 TV Antenna, Outdoor, Amplified, 75 Mile Range, Durable Lightweight, Mount Kit Included, Roof or Attic, 4K-Ready, 30 Foot Detachable Cable, Premium Materials for Performance, MH-110585,Black

text_fidelity_a:
Amcrest ProHD 1080P WiFi 2MP (1920TVL) Indoor Pan/Tilt Security Wireless IP Camera IP2M-841B (Black) UPDATE:
The whole purpose of having a WiFi camera is to put it up in the best place and have it connect via, duh, WiFi.

After finally figuring out how to do that (plug it in temporarily with an ethernet cable, get it to connect via WiFi, then disconnect and relocate the camera) I got it to work. For about a week. For some reason, it "forgets" it's supposed to be on a WiFi network and after a few days simply stops sending the picture to my phone. If I unplug the camera from the wall and reboot, it auto-reconnects, but after a few days, it falls off the network again.

I won't buy another.

Original review:
I received the Amcrest ProHD 1080p IP PT "WiFi" camera yesterday, 10/30/15.

I downloaded the Amcrest Lite iPhone app. Followed instructions. It would not connect via Wi-Fi using my router's password. Tried again and again. I have a TP-Link C9 dual band wireless router with both 5gHz and 2.4gHz transmission. The Amcrest website says in an obscure forum post that the camera operates only in the 2.4gHz band. I changed my iPhone6 (iOS 9.0.2) from 5G to 2.4G. Still could connect via Wi-Fi.

So I plugged the camera directly into the router via ethernet, completely defeating the purpose for the initial purchase. It finally connected. I saw the picture for about 30 seconds, trying to get the camera to full screen, I clicked around on the mysterious icons. Nothing seemed to work. I clicked on the "X" box. The camera disappeared. I tried to reconnect. It came back with "USER LOCKED." I went to their website to search for an answer. They said (at least for their DVR line -- virtually nothing was about this camera) "users are locked out after two failed logon attempts and that I must wait 30 minutes for the reset." I waited. Still USER LOCKED. No camera. I don't even recall trying to log in. I was in the app, trying to reconnect the camera.

I created my Amcrest user account and received their confirming email. I created a user and password for Amcrest.com. The account is actually for something called amcrest.Zendesk and Accumed.zendesk and Foscamhelp.zendesk. I then tried to log in at Amcrest.com. It won't take my log-on credentials. "Invalid Logon or Password." How many user names and passwords does it take to plug in a camera?

Trying to start over, I deleted the app and rebooted the camera. Still USER LOCKED.

Finally, I found that if you push and hold in the little LED network-activity-indicator button on the back of the camera for 10 seconds, the camera will reset to factory. Deleted the app again, set my phone to operate in the 2.4gHz band. Still won't connect via WiFi. Plugged in via ethernet, then used my router's password and it connected. Per the prompt, I then created a new secure password, replacing the default "admin/admin". Finally, I can see and control the camera. So, I have a WiFi camera that won't WiFi. The camera needs to connect to the router at 2.4gHz band (and in my case, via an ethernet cable) but after getting it set, the phone can go back to the 5G if desired.

They claim their products are "Simple, Reliable, Secure." Not quite. They fail to hook to Wi-Fi and then lock me out. Their website won't let me log on even with a user and password.

I downloaded the camera's big PDF user manual to find what the icons mean. The document looks nothing like the camera's icons. They went into great detail...about a previous firmware version, then changed the firmware to look very differently.

The camera works, eventually, and only via ethernet in some cases, but getting there is a real test of patience.
text_fidelity_b: Amcrest ProHD 1080P WiFi 2MP (1920TVL) Indoor Pan/Tilt Security Wireless IP Camera IP2M-841B (Black)

Mohu Television Antenna Leaf 30 Paper-Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna for Free TV MH-110502 There are so many good reviews here about this antenna, I'll try not to repeat what others have said. I do have a few tips to add,

When setting up your antenna, do yourself a favor and tie a string through the two holes at the top of the antenna. That way you can hang it on one tack/nail as you're searching for the best location. Have extra tacks or nails handy, as they will jump out of your hand and become lost in the carpet (until you find them the next day with a bare foot).

Buy some very small nails. I've discovered that I need to move the antenna around to get reception for some channels. Therefore I have a fair number of nails in the wall that look a little strange. Small nails are less visually distracting. If I get very ambitious, I might even paint them.

This antenna really works best on an exterior wall facing the majority of transmitting antennas you are trying to reach. So if you're working with an interior wall facing the wrong direction, it probably won't work very well.

To up the number of channels you receive, consider buying a signal amplifier (I bought the RCA Digital Amplifier here on Amazon.) They cost about $15. I added 10 additional channels by using one.

Finally, how well these indoor antennas work largely depends on where you live and how close you are to the transmitting antennas. To avoid disappointment, do some research online before purchasing anything.The site that helped me the most was disablemycable.com .
text_fidelity_b: Mohu Television Antenna Leaf 30 Paper-Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna for Free TV MH-110502

text_fidelity_a:
CORSAIR Hydro Series H105 AIO Liquid CPU Cooler, 240mm Thick Radiator, Dual 120mm PWM Fans I've wanted to try one of these liquid CPU coolers for ages, but it always been a little too cheap to spend the extra money on one, and I confess I've been mildly concerned about using a liquid anything inside my computer. I'm glad I tried this out.

This particular model has a radiator style grate which the fan sits on (there is some conductive paste included), then has tubes leading to the cooler unit. The water is totally enclosed in the system, and I can see no danger of leakage. The fan is quiet and unobtrusive.

It has a four pin connector, so if your computer has a four pin connector as well, your computer can control the speed of the fan. However, the four pin connector can also connect to a three pin connector and it works fine, you just lose that extra bit of control.

The one small improvement I'd like to see is that the water/cooling area only goes to one side of the radiator type grate, not around all of the edges, so one side of it will always be hotter than the other. It still disperses heat well, just seems like a less efficient system then it could be.

Lastly, I love the thumbscrews included for installing. I hate dealing with normal screws, and the thumbscrews are such a thoughtful touch that it made me think well of the company for including them.

Overall, if you've been on the fence about testing out one of these new liquid CPU coolers, I don't see any reason not to try out this one. The price is reasonable for what it is, and it looks like a highly effective setup, certainly better than just using a fan.
text_fidelity_b: CORSAIR Hydro Series H105 AIO Liquid CPU Cooler, 240mm Thick Radiator, Dual 120mm PWM Fans

Either way, I'm looking for a better product, and most of the ones in this price range seem to be identical except for the name on the box. Basically, because of even the higher demands (Skype, streaming, etc) you need that strong signal without drops, both ways. This has a feature called MIMO, which instead of the standard adapter that has one antenna for reception, THIS has multiple antennae to accommodate 2 ways, and to reduce drops in data.
Be sure you disable the anti-virus, failure to do so and it just doesn't work. If you periodically lose the signal and require a reboot, then uninstall the driver in utility, and install the driver only. Then use Windows embedded wireless utility to connect to your wireless network.

Go to the manufacturer site for some excellent recommendations, like if there's a reduction in signal after a few months, set the router to a static channel (like 1, 3, 6, or 9).

text_fidelity_a:
museeq Bluetooth Speaker,Portable Wireless Conference Speakerphone Speaker,Waterproof Shower Speaker,Enhanced Bass,Stereo Sound,Shockproof,Dustproof Outdoor Speaker with Powerbank Black Bottom Line - The speaker itself is excellent but Bluetooth can be an irritating technology.

The speaker is lightweight and even has an attached carrying strap. Unlike a lot of lightweight products though, it doesn't feel flimsy or fragile at all. Instead it has a nice, solid, durable feel to it. While I am not an audiophile, the speaker has a deep, rich sound that I really like. It does well with audiobooks, music, and videos.

The problems seem to be with Bluetooth. One major issue is that the sound stutters while using Bluetooth. It's very noticeable when playing music and very irritating when listening to audiobooks. That's happened with every Bluetooth speaker I've ever tried. A google search indicates that it's a common problem related to the amount of information the computer is trying to pump out to the speaker. There's a checklist of possible issues to go through to try to fix the problem but the stuttering seems all too common with this technology.

Another issue involves changing modes on a Bluetooth speaker. To sidestep the stuttering I plugged this speaker into my computer with a standard jack. It worked fine and the sound was good. When I unplugged it to bring the speaker into another room with me, I had to redo my audio settings. When I plugged it back in with the jack, an audiobook played just fine but there was no sound while playing videos. Again, I had to go into the audio settings and fiddle with them to be able to watch a movie. I've had similar issues with other Bluetooth speakers.

If you are a techie you may be able to resolve such things quickly and easily. The less tech adept you are, the more hassle they will be though. Myself, I'm just going to leave the speaker connected to my pc via a good old fashioned jack because I like its sound. Bluetooth? Bah, I haven't got time to bother with it.
text_fidelity_b: museeq Bluetooth Speaker,Portable Wireless Conference Speakerphone Speaker,Waterproof Shower Speaker,Enhanced Bass,Stereo Sound,Shockproof,Dustproof Outdoor Speaker with Powerbank Black
